_metadata.description: Requirement stubs scaffolded from the P0 operational targets.

requirements.title: Campaign record and lifecycle
requirements.description: A campaign is the work context a producer draws from: theme, audience keys, channel mix, acquisition and retention hypotheses, linked SKUs, and status. Activation is gated on evidence — a campaign with no supporting research reference cannot leave proposed. This is the structural replacement for 'prevent campaign sprawl when signal is weak' being stated as a wish. Preserve the evidence-gated campaign lifecycle while allowing campaign-free drafts under an independent project/subject scope; general Vrooli communication and individual-app campaigns retain distinct purpose, audience, hypothesis and offer basis.

validation.notes: A campaign with all required fields and at least one evidence ref activates; the stored record round-trips.
Activating a campaign with zero evidence refs is rejected with a typed error naming the missing input.
CLI campaign create then activate round-trips through Connect and is listed by campaign list.

requirements.title: Artifact slot budget
requirements.description: Each campaign declares its artifact slots by channel and format. Drafts consume slots. A draft request beyond the declared budget is refused rather than queued. The budget is the forcing function that keeps in-flight work bounded by design, which also bounds the operator review load. Collections, family membership and source links do not consume additional slots; charge a draft once to its actual admitted campaign/channel/format. Shared preparation effort is measured separately from slots and counted once.

validation.notes: Creating drafts up to the slot count succeeds; the next create for that campaign is rejected.
Slot occupancy is released when a draft is abandoned and re-consumed by a replacement.
Slot state reported by the campaign read surface matches the drafts actually attached.

requirements.title: Draft lifecycle enforcement
requirements.description: The draft lifecycle is the spine of the scenario and is modelled as a declarative flow contract. Illegal transitions are the product: a draft may not reach approved without passing verification, may not leave published, and may not skip review. The transition table is generated from the contract rather than hand-maintained. Preserve the generated native transition contract and immutable publication history; separate persistence, editorial decision, evidence/media readiness, release and observation dimensions. Corrections, restore-as-new-revision and archival relationships must not rewrite a published historical event.

validation.notes: Every declared state/event pair in the flow contract is exercised against the production transition function.
drafted to approved without an intervening verification pass is rejected.
No transition leaves the published terminal state.
Formal replay of named traces passes against the generated artifact.

requirements.title: Shared claim library
requirements.description: A claim is an assertion that would mislead a reader if false. Claims are first-class records with their own lifecycle, cited by many drafts through a join rather than owned by one. Verify once, cite many. This is what later makes it possible to ask which published posts now carry a false statement. Each citation anchors to the span of draft body it supports. The anchor is P0 because adding it later cannot be backfilled — nobody can reconstruct which sentence an old citation was for — while the coverage view built on it is P1. New citations additionally bind exact body revision, declared offset unit, quoted-span digest/context and source pin; ordered items use stable item identities. Stale or ambiguous anchors are not verified support. Historical unknown anchors are not fabricated by backfill.

validation.notes: A claim cited by two drafts is stored once and resolves from both.
Deleting a draft leaves its cited claims intact and still cited by the remaining drafts.
Claim reuse is visible through the read surface: a claim lists every draft citing it.
A citation persists its span anchor and round-trips; an anchor outside the body length is rejected.

requirements.title: Evidence strength
requirements.description: Evidence has strength. A citation is a path, URL, or receipt id and proves only that someone looked. A check is a stored command plus its expected result and is re-runnable. The two are stored distinctly so the gate can require the stronger form where it is cheap — quantitative, existence, and status claims.

validation.notes: A citation-backed claim and a check-backed claim are distinguishable by evidence kind on read.
A check records command, expected result, last run time, and last observed result.
A quantitative claim carrying only a citation is reported as under-evidenced for its kind.

requirements.title: Verification gate
requirements.description: The central invariant. A draft citing any claim not in the verified state cannot transition to approved, and the refusal names which claims are blocking. Everything else in this scenario is bookkeeping; this is the behaviour that makes the honesty doctrine mechanical.

validation.notes: Approval of a draft with one unverified claim is rejected and the error names that claim.
Approval succeeds once every cited claim reaches verified.
A claim moving from verified to stale returns its citing draft to a blocked state before publication.
The gate holds through the Connect surface, not only in the service layer.

requirements.title: Operator-only approval
requirements.description: Approval is the last human check before a public claim and is never delegated to an agent. The API accepts approval only from an operator identity and records approver, draft, and timestamp as durable attribution. Approval records the acting identity and the capacity it acted in, per D-015; a single-operator install is the case where one actor holds every capacity. Native human-only approval remains distinct from a narrower destination-unbound wording decision and from release authorization. Combined human presentation records each exact scope and separate receipt; agent craft verdicts never satisfy this gate.

validation.notes: An approval attempt carrying a non-operator actor kind is rejected.
A successful approval writes approver identity and timestamp that survive a read round-trip.
Attribution is populated from the request context rather than a client-supplied field.

requirements.title: Post-type registry and activation gate
requirements.description: The post-type registry holds each type's medium, activation state, paired-skill reference, required fields, and declared failure modes. Activation criteria become executable rather than a rule stated in a README, and an inactive type blocks approval of any draft using it. Article and simple-post intake must use a genuinely compatible native type/one-off route or expose the missing activation seam; never spoof an active dev-log/spotlight type. Planning unsupported formats does not activate them.

validation.notes: Each declared activation criterion is evaluated independently and reported per criterion.
A draft whose post type is inactive cannot be approved, and the refusal names the failing criterion.
The registry gate command reports activation state for every registered type.

requirements.title: Review scoring
requirements.description: A review run scores a draft against the failure modes its post type declares, recording a verdict and supporting evidence per mode. This covers both craft failure modes and the AI-UGC policy guardrails — no credential claims by a persona, no real-person likeness, no fabricated customer testimonial, disclosure present where required. Preserve per-type policy/craft scoring. Founder-article route acceptance additionally distinguishes source-aware facts/permissions review from an independent article-only reader-promise, causal-story and payoff review; contributor experience is never generated by review.

validation.notes: A review run records one verdict per declared failure mode for the draft's type.
A run with any failed mode leaves the draft blocked rather than reviewed.
Policy modes are evaluated for persona-voiced drafts and skipped for brand-voiced ones.
Review output is retrievable alongside the draft it scored.

requirements.title: Publish ledger
requirements.description: The publish record is what shipped: draft, channel, URL, platform post id, series membership, and the prior post in that series. It is the read surface future drafts depend on for inter-post linkage, and the input the learning loop has never had. Join reported/verified outcomes through native Channel Manager identities and evidence tiers, preserving exact package/account/item and immutable actual-time history. Copy and schedule are not publication; imported history may retain nullable draft references and no fabricated approval.

validation.notes: A publish record round-trips with series membership and prior-post reference intact.
Querying a series returns its posts in publication order.
Publishing a draft transitions it to published and writes exactly one ledger row.

requirements.title: Subject familiarity state
requirements.description: Subject familiarity answers whether a named subject — a scenario, agent, or concept — has already been introduced to a given audience, so a draft introduces it on first mention and stops re-introducing it afterwards. Only actual authorized publication evidence produces familiarity writeback; import, private copy or draft acceptance does not. Missing familiarity defaults to explanation and visible unknown rather than inferred reader knowledge.

validation.notes: A subject never published to an audience reports as not introduced.
After a publish mentioning that subject, the same query reports introduced with the publishing post.
Familiarity is tracked per audience, so introduction to one audience does not imply another.

requirements.title: Narration ledger
requirements.description: The narration ledger records what has already been said about a given scenario so a later post advances the story instead of repeating it. This is the mechanism behind the dev-log discipline of showing only changes that matter and not narrating every commit.

validation.notes: Narrated items recorded against a subject are returned by a later query for that subject.
A query scoped to a date range returns only what was narrated inside it.
Publishing a draft records its narrated items in one operation with the ledger write.

requirements.title: Idempotent state import
requirements.description: Import is a permanent capability, not a one-shot migration: it performs the initial backfill from the marketing team's existing file-backed state and remains the drift-recovery path. Idempotency is by content-addressed key with a unique index, never by line offset or watermark, because those sources are rewritten and reordered by hand and the first reflow would re-import an entire file as new. Retain this existing file-backed team-state importer and its content-addressed semantics. New article intake and user archive restore are separate bounded adapters with explicit source-version/target/import intent, preview and conflict policies; they do not silently reinterpret append-only historical import.

validation.notes: Importing the same source twice creates rows only on the first pass.
Reordering lines in a source without changing content produces no new rows.
A per-source read failure skips that source and is reported rather than recorded as a complete sweep.
A backfill over the real team state files produces a non-empty ledger and re-runs clean.

requirements.title: Operator workbench
requirements.description: The operator workbench is a three-pane desk: queue, draft editor, and a permanently docked inspector holding claims and review verdicts. Approval must be fast, because operator attention is the binding constraint once agents are freer. A disabled approve control always states its reason inline. A disabled approval control always names its specific cause — an unresolved claim, an inactive post type, or an exhausted slot budget. The accepted Marketing workspace extends the workbench into Today, Plan, Create, Review, Learn and persistent Content with task-specific geometry. Preserve desktop evidence inspection, authoring/review parity, keyboard access and inline specific blocker causes; do not force a queue column into every unrelated task.

validation.notes: The inspector renders claim state and review verdicts for the selected draft.
The approve control is disabled with a stated reason when a claim is unverified, the post type is inactive, or the slot budget is exhausted.
Queue, editor, claim resolution, and approval are reachable by keyboard with visible focus.
A draft moves from queue selection through claim resolution to approval in the running UI.

requirements.title: Draft authoring and revision
requirements.description: The operator composes and revises a draft body inside the workbench rather than in an external editor. This is co-equal with review, not secondary to it: a solo operator who must leave the surface to fix a word breaks the ledger the moment they do. Every revision records whether an operator or a commissioned agent produced it, so agent output is always editable content with visible provenance and never a locked result. Preserve native immutable revisions and actor provenance while admitting external authorship/method pins, revision-guarded edits, exact compare and restore-as-new-revision; good external work is not regenerated as a storage prerequisite.

validation.notes: A revision persists and is retrievable, and its author kind round-trips as operator or agent.
Revising a draft in a terminal status is rejected with a typed error.
The editor renders an existing body, accepts an edit, and persists it without leaving the workbench.
The editor is reachable and operable by keyboard alone, with a visible focus state.
